# $2K → $100K in 90 Days — The T^Rock Execution Plan

**Window:** September 1 – November 30 (peak post-storm / pre-winter close season)
**Starting capital:** $2,000
**Target:** $100,000 in gross profit collected, generated by activity this plan starts
**Vehicle:** Selling and producing roofs — the business you already run

---

## Why this is the play (and not something else)

With $2,000 and 90 days there are only a few honest ways to 50x money.
Trading, crypto, and gambling are negative-expectation lotteries at this
timescale — anyone promising otherwise is selling something. Buying and
flipping product caps out around 2–3x per cycle with real risk of dead
inventory. The one asset that legitimately 50x's small money is **a skill
that closes high-ticket sales, applied at maximum volume** — and roofing
insurance restoration is one of the highest-ticket, fastest-cycle sales
that exists. You already have the license context, the process, the CRM,
the pitch materials, and the season. The $2,000 isn't the engine; it's
the fuel for lead flow. **You are the engine.**

## The math (so the target is real, not vibes)

Assumptions — adjust in the scorecard if your actuals differ:

| Input | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Average residential replacement (contract value) | $14,000 |
| Gross margin at 2.0× markup (after materials, labor, dumpster, permit) | ~40% |
| Gross profit per job | ~$5,600 |
| Supplements uplift (realistic, itemized) | +10–20% claim value on most insurance jobs |

**$100,000 gross profit ÷ $5,600/job ≈ 18 jobs closed *and collected* in 90 days = 1.5 closings/week.**

If the target is $100k in *signed contract value* instead, that's only
**7–8 jobs** — you could hit that in the first month alone. This plan aims
at the harder number.

The funnel that produces 18 collected jobs (standard storm-restoration
conversion rates, door-to-door on storm-affected streets):

| Stage | Rate | Weekly volume needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Doors knocked | — | 400 (≈ 20/hr × 4 hrs/day × 5 days) |
| Conversations | ~30% answer | 120 |
| Inspections booked | ~15% of conversations | 18 |
| Claims filed / proposals sent | ~50% of inspections | 9 |
| Approved & signed | ~50% | 4–5 |
| Collected (lags 3–5 weeks behind signing) | — | ramps to 2+/wk by week 6 |

Signings weeks 1–8 become collections weeks 4–12. Front-load the knocking:
**every door you don't knock in September is a job you can't collect in November.**

---

## The $2,000 budget

Spend nothing that doesn't directly create conversations with homeowners.

| Item | Cost | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2,500 door hangers (storm-damage inspection offer + QR to site) | $250 | Left at every no-answer — doubles effective door coverage |
| 50 yard signs + stakes ("Another roof by T^Rock" + phone) | $350 | One at every build and every signed job; each active jobsite sells the street |
| Google Local Services Ads (pay-per-lead, "Google Guaranteed") | $600 | Highest-intent inbound leads available; ~$60–100/lead; turn on Sept 1 |
| Facebook/Nextdoor hyperlocal ads (storm-date targeted, 5-mile radius) | $300 | Run *only* in the 72 hours after a hail/wind event in your area |
| Hail-swath data (HailTrace or equivalent, 3 months) | $300 | Knock only streets that actually got hit — this is what makes 15% inspection rates possible |
| 500 referral cards ("$250 for any referral that becomes a roof") | $75 | Bounty itself is paid out of job proceeds, not this budget |
| Domain + polished lead-capture on the site (Pages hosting is free) | $25 | Where the QR codes, ads, and GBP all point |
| Reserve / reprints / gas money for canvassers | $100 | — |
| **Total** | **$2,000** | |

**Do not spend on:** shared lead resellers (Angi/HomeAdvisor-type — recycled
leads sold to 4 competitors), generic brand ads, or anything that isn't a
homeowner conversation. And **never offer to eat a deductible** — it's
insurance fraud in most states and one caught instance erases the whole 90 days.

## Week-by-week

### Week 0 (first 3 days) — infrastructure, all free
- Deploy this repo to GitHub Pages; put the CRM at `/crm/` in daily use — every
  lead goes in same-day, pipeline stages run the playbooks automatically.
- Google Business Profile: complete every field, add 30 job photos from
  CompanyCam, first post, enable messaging. GBP is the #1 free lead source.
- Send the "final email" review-ask to every past customer not yet asked —
  every review compounds all paid spend for the rest of the plan.
- Order hangers, signs, referral cards. Apply for Google Local Services
  (verification takes days — start immediately).
- Pull hail-swath maps for the last 12 months; rank neighborhoods by
  (storm severity × roof age × your drive time). Build the knock list.

### Weeks 1–4 — VOLUME. Nothing else matters.
- **4 hours of doors daily, 6 days/week**, on swath streets only. Hanger at
  every no-answer, return pass 3 days later at a different time of day.
- Same-day inspection whenever the homeowner allows. Photos → CompanyCam →
  inspection summary sent *that evening* (speed is the differentiator).
- File claims with the homeowner on the spot when damage is real; log
  carrier/claim#/adjuster in the CRM insurance card.
- **Be at every adjuster meeting.** Approval rate with you on the roof vs.
  not is the single biggest swing in this whole plan.
- Yard sign the moment a contract signs. Ask for referrals at signing, not
  just at closeout — hand them 5 cards.
- Target: 16 weeks' worth of knocking compressed into 4. **20+ signed by week 4.**

### Weeks 5–8 — convert and compound
- Mornings: production oversight + adjuster meetings + supplements
  (itemized: ice & water, drip edge, steep/high charges, O&P where legit —
  every approved supplement dollar is margin).
- Afternoons: keep knocking (min. 200 doors/week) + run every referral within 24h.
- Collect on schedule: deductible/first check at signing, balance at final
  invoice — the CRM claim ledger shows exactly what each carrier still owes;
  chase depreciation checks weekly.
- Closeout machine: CompanyCam report → final email → review ask → referral
  ask on every completed job. Reviews + signs + referrals now generate leads
  at $0 acquisition cost.

### Weeks 9–12 — collect and close the year-end angle
- Pitch every open proposal on urgency that's actually true: winter is coming,
  crews book out, insurance approvals have deadlines.
- Sweep every job in Insurance/Approved stages for uncollected supplements
  and recoverable depreciation — this sweep alone is typically worth
  $10–20k across 18 jobs.
- Push everything buildable into production before hard weather; anything
  signed but not buildable, collect the first check and schedule.
- Reinvest: when GLSA leads are converting, top the budget up from collected
  profit — the $2k cap was the seed constraint, not a spending rule.

## Scripts (word-for-word starters)

**Door:** "Hi — I'm Dom with T^Rock. We're doing the insurance work on
[neighbor's street/name] from the [month] hailstorm. Most roofs on this
street took the same hit — I'm doing free 15-minute inspections with photo
documentation while I'm here. If there's damage, your insurance likely owes
you a roof; if there isn't, I'll tell you that too and you'll have the
photos on file. Takes 15 minutes — I can do it right now."

**Referral (at signing and at closeout):** "Best part of my job is I never
have to advertise much — it's mostly neighbors. Anyone you know with a roof
that took this storm? I pay $250 for any referral that turns into a job,
and I'll treat them exactly like I treated you."

**Adjuster meeting:** be on the roof first, chalk and photograph every hit,
walk the adjuster to your marks, agree on scope line-by-line, get the
verbal on the spot, log everything in the CRM before leaving the driveway.

## Weekly scorecard (fill in every Sunday — the plan self-corrects)

| Week | Doors | Inspections | Claims filed | Signed ($) | Collected ($) | GP collected ($) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | | | | | | |
| … | | | | | | |

Rules: if inspections < 15/wk → the problem is doors (volume or wrong
streets). If signings < 40% of inspections → the problem is the pitch or
claim quality (ride along with your best closer for a day). If collections
lag signings by > 5 weeks → the problem is production scheduling or check
chasing, and it's fixed with phone calls, not more leads.

## Honest risk notes

- **The gate is storms.** A dead-quiet fall cuts the insurance funnel;
  the fallback is retail re-roofs and repairs off GLSA + GBP + referrals —
  same funnel, smaller tickets, and the $500-minimum repair pipeline keeps
  cash moving.
- **Collections lag.** $100k *signed* is nearly certain on this activity
  level; $100k *collected in-window* depends on carriers and crew capacity.
  Everything signed by week 8 with checks chased weekly gets there.
- **The plan fails only at the doors.** Every conversion rate above is
  ordinary. 400 doors a week is not.
